do_not_conclude: Do not conclude that the instrument can distinguish stage failure from data loss in real cascading scenarios.

findings.claim: Stage probes are isolated but may be tautological if they directly encode the fault label.
findings.fix: Provide probe construction details and ensure probes are not derived from the fault labels; use held-out independent annotations.
findings.why: The contract defines stage-specific probes (F0-F5) and reports perfect accuracy, but without independent annotation or a description of how probes are constructed, it is possible that the probes trivially reveal the fault type.

findings.claim: No control for cascading failures or end-to-end traces.
findings.fix: Add end-to-end traces with cascading failures and evaluate whether the instrument can localize the root cause.
findings.why: The boundary admits that causal localization from a single cascading trace is not solved, yet the instrument claims to distinguish stage failure from data loss. Without end-to-end tests, the distinction may be artificial.

minimum_next_action: Add end-to-end cascading failure traces and independent annotations.

do_not_conclude: Do not conclude that the instrument estimates real localization accuracy without these controls.

findings.claim: Missing cases include single-fault, no-fault, and cascading-failure scenarios.
findings.fix: Include single-fault, no-fault, and cascading-failure cases in the evaluation set.
findings.why: The summary reports only multi-fault and missing-telemetry cases; without single-fault and no-fault controls, the reported accuracies may be inflated or uninterpretable.

minimum_next_action: Expand the case set to include single-fault and no-fault controls.

do_not_conclude: Do not conclude that B3 is superior to B1/B2 without controlling for confounds.

findings.claim: B1/B2 and B3 are not directly comparable because B3 uses rule-based entity-time extraction while B1/B2 are generic retrieval.
findings.fix: Control for query understanding by providing the same entity/time extraction to all baselines or compare within the same retrieval paradigm.
findings.why: B3 has access to entity and time parsing rules, giving it an advantage on time-related queries; B1/B2 do not. The comparison conflates retrieval backend with query understanding.

findings.claim: The gold-evidence oracle (O) achieves perfect scores, but it is not independent and may leak labels.
findings.fix: Use independently annotated gold evidence and ensure the oracle does not have access to answer labels.
findings.why: The oracle is authored by the same project agent and is not independent gold; its perfect performance is expected and does not validate the task.

findings.claim: Forbidden intrusion rate is 1 for B1/B2, indicating they always retrieve forbidden evidence, but this may be an artifact of the metric definition.
findings.fix: Clarify the forbidden intrusion metric and ensure it is meaningful for the task.
findings.why: Without a clear definition of 'forbidden intrusion', a rate of 1 could mean the metric is too strict or the baselines are not designed to avoid such intrusions.

minimum_next_action: Redesign the comparison to control for query understanding and use independent gold.

do_not_conclude: Do not conclude that the curve represents a general improvement trend.

findings.claim: The update-count curve may be confounded by query category distribution and backend capabilities.
findings.fix: Analyze the curve per query category and control for query difficulty.
findings.why: The curve likely reflects that B1/B2 fail on natural-language and relative-time queries, while B3 succeeds on unseen-current and unseen-iso-time. This is not a smooth learning curve but a step function due to rule coverage.

minimum_next_action: Report per-category curves and control for query difficulty.

do_not_conclude: Do not conclude any architecture validity from this development-only evidence.

findings.claim: All evidence is authored-challenge-development-only with no independent annotation.
findings.fix: Obtain independent annotations and run a blind evaluation on a held-out set.
findings.why: The status explicitly states 'independent_annotation: false', so any architecture claim is unsupported.

findings.claim: The summary claims perfect accuracies, but these are on a small, self-authored set.
findings.fix: Increase case count and diversity, and use statistical significance testing.
findings.why: Perfect scores on 16 cases do not generalize; the boundary admits limitations.

minimum_next_action: Conduct an independent blind evaluation with external annotators.
